record.paper_title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
record.context_brief: General expressibility problem for language-building systems
record.original_question: Fix a finite alphabet A, choose a basis B of languages over A, choose a collection of operations on languages, and choose rules governing how those operations may be applied. Which languages over A can be expressed from the basis B by using the chosen operations according to those rules?

evidence.quote:
The aim of this paper is to discuss various instances of the following general problem.
Problem. Given a “basis” of languages, a set of operations and some rules
to use them, describe the languages expressible from the basis by using the
operations according to the rules.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let A* denote the free monoid of all finite words over A. A language over A is a subset of A*. Fix:

(i) a family B of languages over A, called the basis;
(ii) a collection O of operations on languages over A (each operation taking a tuple of languages and producing a language, e.g. union, intersection, complement, concatenation, Kleene star, inverse homomorphism, quotient by a word, etc.);
(iii) a set R of formal rules governing how the operations in O may be combined and iterated (for instance, restrictions on alternation depth, on the use of complement, or on the form of allowed compositions).

Say that a language L ⊆ A* is expressible from (B, O, R) if L can be obtained by starting from members of B and applying operations from O in a manner that conforms to the rules R.

General expressibility problem: Give an explicit, decidable characterization of the class of all languages L ⊆ A* that are expressible from (B, O, R), for any specified choice of (B, O, R).

Concrete instance to address: provide a procedure that, given finite descriptions (e.g. by finite automata) of a language L and of the basis B, together with the specification of O and R, decides whether L is expressible from (B, O, R), or prove that no such procedure exists.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a general framework problem encompassing many classical questions about regular languages (Schützenberger's theorem on star-free languages, dot-depth hierarchy, concatenation hierarchies, etc.). Many specific instances remain open, notably the decidability of higher levels of the Straubing–Thérien and dot-depth hierarchies; recent progress has been made (e.g., decidability of level 2 by Place and Zeitoun, 2014–2019) but the general problem as a whole remains open.

status_evidence.title: Going Higher in the First-order Quantifier Alternation Hierarchy on Words
status_evidence.snippet: Place and Zeitoun prove decidability of membership for level 2 of the Straubing–Thérien hierarchy, leaving higher levels open.
status_evidence.claim: Specific instances of the general expressibility problem for regular languages remain open at higher hierarchy levels.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems concerning the expressibility of regular languages from a basis using operations under rules.
status_evidence.claim: The general framework problem is presented as a guiding open problem in the theory of regular languages.
